title: Fix broken update-declarative-config step and :latest image tags in drawrace-build WorkflowTemplate
description:
Plan ref: docs/plan/plan.md §Multiplayer & Backend 10 (Deployment) and §Testing 11 (CI Pipeline). File: k8s/drawrace-build-workflowtemplate.yml (in-repo copy of the iad-ci template; after fixing, sync to declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ via git commit+push — never kubectl apply directly).

Four concrete defects in the update-declarative-config template (around lines 474-496) plus the Kaniko step (~line 618):

1. Docker Hub org typo: line ~490 writes 'ronaldrayrun/drawrace-live:latest' into images.txt — should be 'ronaldraygun'. As-is it publishes a nonexistent image ref (ImagePullBackOff downstream).
2. Stray YAML fragment inside the shell script: lines ~495-496 end with 'git push' followed by an orphaned 'key: token' line INSIDE the block scalar — the shell executes 'key: token' as a command and the step exits nonzero. This is a remnant of missing secret env wiring: the git clone is anonymous https to git.ardenone.com, so the push has no credentials at all and would 401 even without the stray line. Wire a token from a secret (see how docker-build wires github-webhook-secret) and embed it in the push URL.
3. ':latest' everywhere: images.txt lines are fixed ':latest' strings, and the Kaniko docker-build template pushes only '--destination={{inputs.parameters.image}}:latest'. This violates the workspace convention 'never use :latest image tags' AND makes the bump a permanent no-op: images.txt content never changes between builds, so 'git diff --cached --quiet' always short-circuits the commit and ArgoCD never sees a new tag. Fix: push an immutable tag (git short SHA) from Kaniko and write the SHA-tagged refs into declarative-config.
4. Git identity: template commits as 'DrawRace CI <ci@drawrace.ardenone.com>' — convention requires user.name jedarden, user.email github@jedarden.com for all CI auto-bumps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Kaniko pushes ronaldraygun/drawrace-{api,validator,live} with a git-SHA tag (optionally also :latest, but manifests/images.txt must reference the SHA tag).
- update-declarative-config script is valid sh (no stray YAML lines), authenticates the push via a secret env, uses the jedarden git identity, and produces a real commit when the SHA changes.
- Org typo fixed (ronaldraygun).
- Repo copy k8s/drawrace-build-workflowtemplate.yml updated first, then the same content committed+pushed to declarative-config so ArgoCD syncs it (do not mutate the live cluster directly).

description:
The rotate-client-key step in drawrace-build WorkflowTemplate runs kubectl using the pod's in-cluster SA token (iad-ci cluster), but tries to access drawrace namespace which doesn't exist on iad-ci.

The step is meant to update drawrace-client-key ConfigMap on iad-acb (the deployment target), not iad-ci.

Fix options (pick one):
A. Add a kubeconfig secret for iad-acb to argo-workflows namespace on iad-ci, then mount it in the rotate-client-key step and use KUBECONFIG env var.
B. Change rotate-client-key to commit the new key value to declarative-config (k8s/iad-acb/drawrace/api-deployment.yaml) and let ArgoCD propagate it — avoids needing cross-cluster kubectl in CI.
C. Use the existing iad-acb SA token (from iad-acb-readonly.kubeconfig) — create a new SA with write access to drawrace namespace, store its token as a secret in iago-workflows on iad-ci.

Option A is simplest. Steps:
1. Create a ServiceAccount in iad-acb/drawrace namespace with Role that allows get/apply on configmaps
2. Extract its token
3. Create a kubeconfig secret in iad-ci argo-workflows namespace pointing to iad-acb
4. Update the rotate-client-key template in drawrace-build WorkflowTemplate to mount the secret and use KUBECONFIG

Note: this is P1 (not blocking pod startup, only HMAC key rotation on each deploy).

Acceptance: rotate-client-key node shows Succeeded in next drawrace-build run.
